result.summary: Adds an `auto_outbound_mode` setting to the functional test framework and introduces a new test script `p2p_outbound_management.py`. In this mode, the node under test is allowed to autonomously initiate outbound connections to addresses in addrman via a SOCKS5 proxy that redirects them to Python P2P peers or other test nodes. The PR also refactors `p2p_private_broadcast.py` to use the shared test framework implementation instead of its own custom proxy redirect logic.
result.problem: P2P logic where bitcoind autonomously chooses when and where to initiate outbound connections has historically lacked functional test coverage because standard tests establish connections inward or use manual `add_outbound_p2p_connection` calls. Important outbound connection management behaviors—such as opening an extra connection on a stale tip, periodic block-relay-only peer rotation, and network diversification—could not be easily tested end-to-end.
evidence: PR description notes that auto_outbound_mode 'allows to test the code in which the node decides to make connections - in contrast to the existing add_outbound_p2p_connection where the functional test initiates the connections.'

Adds functional test coverage for previously uncovered or under-tested outbound P2P mechanisms merged across multiple past PRs: stale tip extra connection (#11560), periodic block-relay-only connections (#19858), and network diversification (#27213).
result.scope_notes: The PR extracts and generalizes SOCKS5 redirection machinery introduced in #29415 into `BitcoinTestFramework`, converts `p2p_private_broadcast.py` to use it, and adds the new test `p2p_outbound_management.py`.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided matches the scope of the previous description; no structural changes to the commits or implementation approach.
result.card: Adds an auto_outbound_mode helper to the functional test framework and introduces functional test coverage for automatic outbound connection management. Functional tests typically rely on the test runner manually initiating connections, leaving the node's autonomous outbound connection decisions untested in an end-to-end environment. By routing autonomous addrman connections through a SOCKS5 proxy back to controllable Python P2P test peers, this PR exercises stale-tip extra connection logic, scheduled block-relay-only peer probing, and network diversification across IPv4, Tor, and CJDNS. It also dedupes test proxy logic previously isolated inside p2p_private_broadcast.py.

risk.why: Only touches Python functional tests and test framework utilities; any bug would result in flaky CI runs or failed tests without affecting production node behavior.
